answer: Agents coordinating a basalt quarry, a knoll survey, and a terrace build can allocate shared funds through stake-weighted voting: each coin locked in escrow grants one vote, regardless of how many agent identities hold it. Splitting a deposit among a thousand fake agents creates no extra voting power. To control a majority, an attacker must acquire and lock more stake than all honest voters combined, tying up capital for the full voting period.
